evidence.intree_statement: Context {C D : Category} {F : D ⟶ C} {U : C ⟶ D}.  Theorem Adjunction_Monad : F ⊣ U → @Monad D (U ◯ F).
Class LocalRightKan (X : A ⟶ C) := { LocalRan : B ⟶ C; ran_transform : LocalRan ◯ F ⟹ X; ump_ran (M : B ⟶ C) (μ : M ◯ F ⟹ X) : (∃! δ, μ ≈ ran_transform ∙ δ ⊲ F) }.
Definition Adjunction_Induced_Monad : @Monad D (U ◯ F) := @Build_Monad D (U ◯ F) (fun x => @unit _ _ _ _ A x) (fun x => fmap[U] (@counit _ _ _ _ A (F x))) ... (* ret = η, join = U ε F *)

statement_record.book: For G : D ⟶ C the codensity monad is T := Ran_G G, the right Kan extension of G along ITSELF (when it exists, e.g. as a pointwise Kan extension when C has enough limits), with 2-cell ε : TG ⟹ G; the unit η : id_C ⟹ T and multiplication μ : T² ⟹ T are the unique factorizations through ε of id_G and of the pasted double-ε composite. Preceding prose: a right adjoint G with left adjoint F induces the monad GF, and a general G still induces a monad on C via Ran_G G.
statement_record.intree: Theorem Adjunction_Monad : F ⊣ U → @Monad D (U ◯ F).  Class LocalRightKan (X : A ⟶ C) := { LocalRan : B ⟶ C; ran_transform : LocalRan ◯ F ⟹ X; ump_ran (M : B ⟶ C) (μ : M ◯ F ⟹ X) : (∃! δ, μ ≈ ran_transform ∙ δ ⊲ F) }.  (Also Class RightKan := { Ran : [A,C] ⟶ [B,C]; ran_adjoint : Induced ⊣ Ran }.)
statement_record.strength_comparison: intree-weaker: only the adjoint special case and the raw machinery are in force. The clause 'a right adjoint induces the monad GF' is fully proved twice (Adjunction_Monad from the hom-set form, Adjunction_Induced_Monad transparently with ret = η, join = U ε F), and right Kan extensions are defined both globally (Ran, as the right adjoint to precomposition) and locally with exactly the universal property the book's η/μ factorizations use (ump_ran gives the unique δ factoring μ through the counit). But nothing in-tree instantiates the extension at X := G along F := G, and no monad structure is derived from ε : Ran_G G ◯ G ⟹ G. The word 'codensity' appears in the tree only in the Theory/Kan/Extension.v header prose (lines 35, 39, 83, 103, 105, 108), never in a statement.

evidence.intree_statement: Definition coyoneda_reduction : coend_obj (SetsCoend YoI) ≅[Sets] F c := coyoneda_iso.   (* with YoI : C^op ∏ C ⟶ Sets, YoI (x,y) = C(x,c) × F y, i.e. ∫^x C(x,c) × F x ≅ F c *)

Lemma coy_cowedge : Cowedge_cond YoI (F c) coy_leg.   (* coy_leg (x) : C(x,c) × F x ~> F c is (g, a) ↦ fmap[F] g a — the cocone leg at x, and coy_cowedge is its compatibility (co-dinaturality) condition *)
Lemma coend_ump (E : Coend F) (w : D) (i : ∀ x : C, F (x, x) ~{D}~> w) (cond : Cowedge_cond w i) : ∃! u : coend_obj E ~{D}~> w, ∀ x : C, u ∘ coend_inj E ≈ i x.

statement_record.book: Use the Yoneda lemma to define the colimit cone for the canonical colimit of Theorem 6.5.7 — i.e. exhibit the cocone whose legs go from the representables indexed by (the opposite of) the category of elements of F to F, witnessing F = colim of that diagram of representables.
statement_record.intree: Lemma coy_cowedge : Cowedge_cond YoI (F c) coy_leg, where coy_leg x : C(x,c) × F x ~> F c is (g,a) ↦ fmap[F] g a; together with Definition coyoneda_reduction : coend_obj (SetsCoend YoI) ≅[Sets] F c and the colimit-style universal property Lemma coend_ump ... : ∃! u : coend_obj E ~> w, ∀ x, u ∘ coend_inj E ≈ i x.
statement_record.strength_comparison: intree-weaker: the density cocone exists only in pointwise coend form. The legs coy_leg x — defined exactly by the Yoneda recipe (g, a) ↦ F(g)(a), which IS the cone the exercise asks for — are indexed by objects x of C with the cowedge (co-dinaturality) condition standing in for functoriality over the category of elements, and the apex is the SET F c rather than the presheaf F. The universal property is the coend UMP (coend_ump), a genuine colimit-style ∃! over cowedges. The book's formulation lives in the functor category ([C,Set]-valued colimit of a diagram of representables indexed by (∫F)^op) and that formulation is not in the tree.
